eight_lines_around: A sequential procedure chooses a pair (i,j) for the next comparison in each stage and decides the stopping time T.
Upon stopping, the final decision is to choose the global rank R := (R₁,...,R_K)
from the set of all permutations of {1,2,...,K}. The loss function of this sequential design
problem is defined by combining the cost of data collection and the Kendall’s tau distance
Σ_{i<j} I(θ_i>θ_j) I(R_i>R_j) + I(θ_i<θ_j) I(R_i<R_j) + cT,
where the constant c > 0 indicates the relative cost of each comparison and I(·) denotes an indicator function.
Although according to the final decision, our problem seems to be a multi-hypotheses sequential testing problem with adaptive experiment selection
there exist fundamental differences. First, ... the ranking problem ... consists of composite hypotheses.
